subject: Unexpected mid-cycle rate band adjustment affecting apportionment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora AI Billing <billing@auroraai.com>
Date: 2027-10-20T16:12:00Z
Subject: Unexplained rate change reflected in Oct invoice lines

Hi Jordan,

We noticed a material change on our October usage export — a single line item shows a different effective per-token rate and the usage appears to have been re-apportioned across two sub-projects that never changed on our end. Invoice AR-4492 shows a ~0.7% uplift compared to September despite flat traffic.

Can you explain whether Redwood applied any rate band adjustments mid-cycle (around Oct 15)? If so, please send:
- the policy or release note that caused the change
- a line-by-line before/after apportionment of tokens across our project IDs (proj-aurora-core, proj-aurora-analytics)
- raw usage export (CSV) for 2027-10-01 through 2027-10-19

I've attached a trimmed sample export for the affected window. We're trying to reconcile with our finance team; if this is an internal reclassification on Redwood's side we may need an adjustment or credit.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Finance, Aurora AI
billing@auroraai.com
Attachment: aurora_sample_usage_export_20271015-19.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-20T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexplained rate change reflected in Oct invoice lines

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads-up and the sample export. I'm putting this on our billing triage and CC'ing Soojin (billing systems) and Ben (accounts) so we can get a quick diagnostic.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Soojin will run a windowed sampling job against your account ID and compare token attribution pre/post Oct 15.
- We'll pull the release notes for any pricing/rate band work applied to streaming vs. batch tokens in the last 30 days.
- Please confirm the exact project IDs (proj-aurora-core, proj-aurora-analytics) and whether you used any temporary API keys during Oct 10–18. That helps rule out key-mapping reclassification.

We'll aim to provide a provisional breakdown and a proposed remediation (credit or adjustment) within 72 hours. I've also placed a temporary hold in our billing system flag so the invoice won't proceed to collections while we investigate.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-22T14:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexplained rate change reflected in Oct invoice lines — initial findings

Hi Samir — quick update from billing systems after sampling your export and the raw logs. Short summary first:

1) No manual price change was applied to Aurora's tenant ratecard on Oct 15.
2) We rolled a small classification change on 2027-10-15 that adjusted how streaming partial-tokens are bucketed for apportionment across sub-projects when multiple API keys map to the same tenant. This change fixed an undercount edge case for some customers but can produce small rounding shifts for accounts with interleaved API key usage.

What we observed in your sample (proj-aurora-core vs proj-aurora-analytics):
- A cluster of ~9k streaming calls from Oct 12–16 were reclassified from the "core" key to the "analytics" key due to a recent key-namespace reconciliation we ran on Oct 15. The reconciliation is deterministic but changes bucket assignment when two keys share a legacy mapping.
- The change results in a ~0.45% effective token uplift for the period you shared because the analytics key has slightly different token-characterization (higher measured tokens per call) and rounding rules.

Next actions we propose:
- We can provide the full per-request line export for 2027-10-10 → 2027-10-19 showing original key, reconciled key, raw token counts, and resulting per-line billable tokens.
- If this reconciliation caused an unintended reallocation for Aurora (i.e., you never intended to map call set B to analytics), we will propose a retroactive apportionment and a pro-rated credit for the affected window.

What we need from you to finalize:
- Confirm the authoritative project IDs and whether the analytics key should be treated as part of the same billing entity as core (some customers prefer separate billing).
- Confirm whether any short-lived API keys were issued Oct 10–16 for internal testing.

I'll prepare the detailed export and a reconciliation plan. Jordan/Ben will follow up with formal credit numbers.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Billing Systems Lead, Redwood Inference
